Better to choose one facet: "Establish the birthplace (place) of the target person and whether it is located in a country whose official website reports a 5.88% population increase between 2010 and 2020." This combines place and demographic but it's one relation: birthplace satisfies demographic. However still requires identify target person? It says person who was born... Might be okay.

Need ensure not a search query. So phrasing as objective.

This is one coherent evidence objective: find the place/country with that demographic statistic. It doesn't require knowing the person. Then later link to birth. This seems a good exploratory facet. It preserves the condition "place population increased by 5.88% between 2010 and 2020 according to official website of country where located." The local residual: "Identify the place and its country for which an official website of that country reports a 5.88% population increase between 2010 and 2020, as the birthplace condition in R2." But wait, there may be many places. The requirement says "a place in which..." not necessarily identify all. But as objective, find candidate place(s). That's one coherent part. It doesn't include birth years. Is that okay? The parent requirement has birth between 1948 and 1952 and place condition. The demographic condition is a distinct semantic condition. Since no claims, it's unresolved. Choose it.

Alternatively choose "Establish that the target person was born between 1948 and 1952." But we don't know target person. The demographic place condition is more self-contained because can research places with 5.88% population growth. The question says "according to one official website of the country in which it is located." So there is a place with that demographic. We can identify it. That seems a low-commitment facet. However, the local residual should be an evidence objective inside R2. It can be "Determine which place experienced a population increase of 5.88% between 2010 and 2020, according to an official website of its country, as the birthplace condition in R2." That is one coherent objective. It doesn't mention person birth years, but that's okay as one facet.

So local_residual: "Establish the identity of the place that serves as the target person's birthplace by determining which place had a population increase of 5.88% between 2010 and 2020 according to an official website of the country in which that place is located." This includes "target person's birthplace" but target person not established. Is that jumping? It says "the place that serves as the target person's birthplace" presupposes target person. But parent requirement is about person born in that place. It's okay. But if target person unknown, maybe we can say "Establish which place, if any, satisfies the 5.88% population increase between 2010 and 2020 according to an official website of its country, as the birthplace condition for the person in R2." That's fine.

But "if any" might be search? No, it's objective.
